text: Phosphorus-starved wheat roots broadcast a diffusible strigolactone signal across a 0.45 um membrane that significantly enhances arbuscular mycorrhizal colonization in unstressed neighboring wheat.
The diffusible strigolactone cue induces significant transcriptional upregulation of the mycorrhiza-specific phosphate transporter TaPT4 in recipient roots prior to recipient phosphorus deficiency.
Chemical inhibition of donor strigolactone biosynthesis using 1 uM Tis-108 completely abolishes the diffusible priming effect in recipient wheat.
Priming of mycorrhizal colonization in recipient wheat strictly requires an intact TaD14 perception receptor in recipient tissues.
Common Mycorrhizal Networks (30 um mesh) provide an additive amplification over diffusible solute transport alone, increasing recipient AM colonization to 54.81%.
Solid partition barriers (M0) completely isolate donor and recipient compartments with zero detectable baseline priming or nutrient leakage.
Strigolactone rhizosphere priming results in accelerated total shoot phosphorus acquisition in unstressed recipient wheat.
